summary:
**Inside the Burn** is an AI-powered interactive dashboard developed by Team Firewall for NASA's Flame in Freefall challenge.

Our project makes microgravity combustion research easier to access, understand, and compare. It organizes selected NASA experiment reports, scientific data, and videos into a searchable platform, allowing users to quickly find experiments by material, test conditions, or experiment ID.

The platform uses AI to generate evidence-based summaries, compare experimental results, explain flame behavior, and provide references to original research sources.

Our goal is to reduce the time researchers spend navigating complex scientific documents and help them identify meaningful findings more efficiently.

Inside the Burn transforms scattered scientific information into an accessible, user-friendly research experience, supporting a better understanding of fire behavior in microgravity and spacecraft fire safety.
details:
Inside the Burn — Team Firewall

Project Overview

Inside the Burn is an interactive, AI-powered research dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the "Flame in Freefall" challenge.

The project helps researchers, students, and engineers explore and interpret microgravity combustion research from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository.

What Does Our Project Do?

Inside the Burn brings scientific information from multiple NASA research records into one accessible platform.

Users can:

  • Search and filter experiments by material, investigation, and experimental conditions.
  • Explore documented combustion experiments, measurements, observations, and available videos.
  • Compare experimental outcomes across different test conditions.
  • Generate AI-assisted Evidence Briefs that summarize findings and reference the original scientific sources.
  • Identify missing information and distinguish documented observations from interpretations.

A practical example is comparing PMMA combustion tests, including B1 and B6, to explore differences in flame behavior and the effects of experimental conditions.

What Problem Are We Solving?

NASA has accumulated extensive microgravity combustion research across scientific reports, experimental records, and multimedia resources.

Finding, understanding, and comparing relevant information can require navigating multiple documents and datasets.

Inside the Burn aims to reduce this research effort by making relevant evidence searchable, comparable, and easier to interpret.

Technology and Development

Our team developed a browser-based application combining an interactive dashboard, structured scientific records, data-processing logic, and AI-assisted research tools.

We used ChatGPT and Cursor as development assistants for programming, debugging, organizing technical information, and improving the research interface.

The application connects experimental information to source references and provides a structured workflow for exploring and comparing evidence.

Creativity and Innovation

Our approach focuses on turning scattered scientific information into an interactive research experience.

Rather than presenting only static PDF files or isolated datasets, the platform combines experiment discovery, contextual comparison, scientific explanations, and source-linked AI summaries.

Its principal innovation is the integration of these capabilities into one research workflow, helping users move from a scientific question to the relevant experimental evidence.

Intended Impact

Inside the Burn aims to improve access to microgravity combustion research, reduce time spent searching scientific records, support scientific education, and assist researchers in exploring evidence relevant to spacecraft fire safety.

The project is a research-support prototype. It does not claim to predict fire behavior in real time, replace scientific validation, or autonomously control fire suppression systems.

Our long-term vision is to make complex space research more accessible, transparent, and useful for scientists, engineers, and future generations of students.
